title: Book One · Chapter 147: What the Box Does Not Say
story:
Leo wants something real beside the map. Mr Qiu's empty pencil box is small. Mum's bag is useful. But Leo wants more real things in the room. Only paper may make it feel like another lesson.

“We have pictures,” Ronan says.

“Paper pictures.”

“We are at school.”

“Yes. I want something besides paper.”

They sit on the floor beside the room plan. Mei has drawn a space for objects on the table. Each object needs a name card. The card must explain the object. Miss Wu wants visitors to understand each object. The cards must explain each thing. Visitors cannot pick everything up.

Ronan thinks of the blue tool box. It is too heavy to carry for the display. Dad needs it. There are sharp tools inside. The box must stay shut at the display. Dad must agree to lend it too. A child might touch a sharp tool inside.

“A picture of the box,” he says.

Leo leans back. “More paper.”

Ronan feels hot. He knows Dad can make and mend things. He wants Leo to see that. He wants to show their old home and shop too. They lived there before the green gate.

“Dad had his own shop,” he says.

“I know.”

“We could tell that story.”

Mei lifts her pencil. “Has he agreed?”

Ronan looks at the list. WAIT is still beside the old-home drawing.

“Not yet.”

Leo takes the small pencil box and turns it over. “Ask him. My father will not lend his work keys either. I already asked.”

Ronan thought Leo could get things easily from his parents. He looks up.

“Why not?”

“Because they are keys. He needs them.”

Ronan looks at him. He thought Leo's parents could always give him things. Now he knows they say no too. Leo's father needs his keys, just as Dad needs tools.

At home he begins a card about Dad. He writes: Dad had a shop. Then he adds: Some things went wrong. Our family moved. He does not write about Dad's old mistakes. He thinks Dad will like the card better that way.

Mum comes in. “May I read it?” she asks. Ronan says yes, and she reads it. She is quiet. Ronan waits for her to speak. Ronan waits a little longer. He feels more worried now.

“He must see this first,” she says.

“I am not putting it up yet.”

“Good.”

“It says he still works well.”

“He may want to keep the old shop story private. Ask him before you show anyone.”

Ronan reads the card again. The old shop fills most of it. Dad's hands, his long workdays, and the invitation in the box are not there at all.

He leaves the card on the table for himself, not on Dad's bowl. He needs to ask while Dad can sit and listen. Tonight Dad has a headache and wants a quiet supper.

He carries the folded card to his own shelf. There is a little space beside the boards. He keeps unfinished papers there. He puts it there. The bell is farther along, beside the red-sail book. He likes having those things at home. He can keep them at home. The bell and book can stay on his shelf.

Ronan fetches water and tells him about Leo's game instead. “Does the blank door have an answer yet?” Dad asks. Ronan says no. Dad says they can leave the answer blank for now. Someone may have an answer for the children. Ronan looks at his folded card and does not unfold it tonight.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：objects＝实物；lend＝借出；private＝私人的。

情节提示：sharp＝锋利的；headache＝头痛；tools＝工具。

理解：1. 为什么工具箱不适合作为开放展品？2. Ronan 写的卡片遗漏了 Dad 的哪些现在生活？
